author: slava77
body:
The primary target is high-pt jet events. This should have an incremental improvement for #51245 

in the 17.0.0pre2 relval GEN-SIM c78d2621-e964-4ec4-baf0-31eb50b6e2bd.root LS:190 had some slow events (4th:5404 7th:5407); a large fraction of time was in the `ExtendT5FromDupT5` kernel. This is partly covered in the discussion thread of #51245 

Two updates were made:
- For the case with `kT5DuplicateMinSharedHits == 8` there is a possible shortcut in the logic where a large fraction of modules or T5s can be skipped early.
- the thread use for cases with modules with many T5s is suboptimal (parallelizes only over modules; as a result only one thread per warp does any work in majority of cases). This part was refactored to collect compatible modules first and then parallelize the loop over T5s rather than the modules.

The updates are expected to be technical (no change in the physics results). The timing/profiling was measured in CMSSW_17_0_0_pre2 after the commits from #51333 (the last relevant change from 20X)

CPU side (using igprof; reference -> 1st change -> 2nd change):
- 10 events from the slow relval 2TeV job (per event): 56.6 s -> 7.0 s -> 6.9 s
- ttbar PU200 benchmark (per event, over 100 evts): 7.70 ms -> 6.60 ms -> 7.2 ms

GPU side is less impressive (times via nsys; reference -> 1st change -> 2nd change):
- 10 events from the slow relval 2TeV job (per event): 3.83 s -> 2.45 s -> 0.228 s
    - the slowest event: 33.8 s -> 21.6 s -> 2.12 s
- ttbar PU200 benchmark (per event, over 100 evts): 0.179 ms -> 0.198 ms -> 0.130 ms

Overall, about a factor of 10 speedup in `ExtendT5FromDupT5` kernel for the high-pt jets (2 TeV events) and some minor speedup in ttbar (this kernel itself was taking about 1/4 of the total LST processing time on CPU)
title: LST: speedup ExtendT5FromDupT5 kernel
